content.value_statement: Godot 3 projects often break after upgrade because GDScript 2.0 changes syntax and APIs. This skill gives focused migration guidance for common upgrade issues.
actual_capabilities: Explains common Godot 3 to Godot 4 syntax changes.
Shows how export, onready, and tool keywords become annotations.
Guides migration from Tween nodes to create_tween usage.
Compares old and new signal connection patterns.
Covers typed arrays, await syntax, and parent method calls.
limitations: Does not run Godot, tests, or project conversion tools.
Does not cover every engine API renamed in Godot 4.
Requires the user to provide project code or error details.
Final migration quality still depends on project-specific testing.

use_cases.title: Upgrade a Small Game Project
use_cases.description: Convert common GDScript patterns before opening the project fully in Godot 4.

use_cases.title: Fix Migration Errors
use_cases.description: Understand errors related to exports, tweens, signals, yield, and typed arrays.
use_cases.target_user: Developer maintaining an existing Godot project

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check whether migration changes follow Godot 4 style and avoid deprecated Godot 3 patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Explain My Upgrade Error
prompt_templates.prompt: I upgraded a Godot 3 project to Godot 4 and see this error: [paste error]. Explain the likely cause and the Godot 4 fix.

prompt_templates.title: Convert GDScript Syntax
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Godot 3 GDScript file for Godot 4 syntax changes. Focus on annotations, signals, tweens, yield, and typed arrays.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration checklist for this Godot 3 project structure. Prioritize changes that commonly block Godot 4 startup.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Migration Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Godot 4 migration diff for missed Godot 3 patterns, risky behavior changes, and tests that should be run.

output_examples.input: A developer asks why a Tween node no longer works after upgrading.
output_examples.output: The response explains that Godot 4 uses tweens created from the scene tree. It recommends replacing node-based tween calls with the new tween object flow and testing timing behavior.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks whether a migrated script still uses old export syntax.
output_examples.output: The response identifies outdated export and onready patterns, explains the annotation replacements, and suggests checking inspector behavior after migration.

output_examples.input: A team asks for a first migration pass checklist.
output_examples.output: The response groups work into syntax cleanup, signal updates, tween migration, coroutine changes, and manual testing inside the Godot editor.

best_practices: Provide the exact Godot version, error message, and related script when asking for help.
Migrate one system at a time and test behavior in the Godot editor after each change.
Use typed variables and Godot 4 signal syntax where it improves clarity.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every Godot 3 API has a direct Godot 4 replacement.
Do not migrate code without running scenes that depend on signals, tweens, or timers.
Do not ignore inspector behavior after changing exported variables.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically convert a full Godot project?
faq.answer: No. It provides migration guidance and review support, but it does not run conversion tools or edit projects automatically.

faq.question: Which Godot versions does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on moving from Godot 3.x to Godot 4 and GDScript 2.0.

faq.question: Can it help with Tween migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the move from Tween nodes to tweens created through create_tween.

faq.question: Can it review signal connection changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares older string-based connections with Godot 4 callable-style connections.

faq.question: Does it replace official Godot documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a focused assistant guide and should be checked against official documentation for edge cases.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Share the script, error message, Godot version, and the scene behavior you expect after migration.
